4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that challenged the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:50589 2 MA-908-2021 award by urging the grounds in appeal that the proper calculation has not been made.

Deceased was of 57 years at the time of death as reflected in the postmortem report Ex-P/7 but the learned claims Tribunal relying on an unexhibited photo copy of Aadhar card has held that the deceased was in the age group of 65 years to 70 years and further on other head also less compensation has been awarded.

5. Learned counsel for the insurance company Shri Rohit Jain had argued that proper compensation has been awarded after taking into consideration of all factual situation.
6. Considered the arguments of learned counsel for rival parties and perused the record.

The learned Tribunal in Para 15 has taken the age of the deceased as 68 year 11 months and 26 days on the date of accident but on perusal of the statement of applicant witnesses namely AW-1 (Smt. Birajo Bai)
and AW/2 (Ghansyam Ahirwar) it reflected that neither the insurance company nor the Tribunal has put any question to the witnesses regarding the age of deceased.
Wife (Smt. Virajo Bai) is an illiterate lady she has put her thumb impression on the deposition sheet.

Further, on perusal of the order sheet, on which the final arguments were heard i.e. 19.01.202, it is seen that learned Tribunal failed to ask any question and record it in order sheet from the counsel , therefore, on the basis of postmortem report the age should have been determine at 57 years accordingly the finding of the learned Tribunal in Para 15 regarding age of the deceased is set aside as a consequences of which the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50589 3 MA-908-2021 calculation of total compensation is also faulty.

Hence, on the basis of aforesaid of 57 years age, the correct calculation of compensation would be as below:-
1

Monthly Income Rs.7375/-
2

Annual income Rs.88,500/- 3 10% towards future prospects Rs.97,350/-
( Rs.88,500/- 10%) 4 Considering number of dependents (1/3) Rs.32,450/-
deduction towards personal expenses ( Rs.97,350/-x 1/3) Family dependency after deduction Rs.64,900/- towards personal living expenses ( Rs.97,350/- - Rs.32,450/-
6 Multiplier considering the age of 9 decease as 57 years 7 Compensation 5as age Rs.5,84,100/-
(Rs.64,900/-x 9)

8 Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- ) 9

Towards funeral expenses + Loss of Rs.30,000/-
estate + (Rs.15,000/-+ Rs.15,000/-) 10
Thus, the total compensation to which the claimant is entitled is Rs. Rs.6,54,100/-
Since the Tribunal has already awarded Rs. Rs.1,60,000/-, therefore, claimant would be entitled to enhancement of compensation of Rs.4,94,100/-(Rs.6,54,100/-- 1,60,000/-)
NEUTRAL
